plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs like SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and stay within single name limits.
Sell QQQ and SMCI due to downtrends and being below stop.
Trim SMH as it is flagged for trimming and in a downtrend.
This plan prioritizes stability and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. However, potential upside is also limited.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to reduce overall leverage.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Sell QQQ due to its downtrend and trim SMH as flagged.
Buy XLV, a top-scoring scanner setup, to diversify and add quality exposure.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF sleeve.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality new setup. Expect moderate drawdowns with a balanced growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Sell QQQ due to its downtrend and trim SMH as flagged.
Increase exposure to leveraged semiconductor ETFs SOXL and MUU.
Buy XLV and AMZN, both strong scanner setups, to add high-conviction growth.
This plan leans into leverage and high-scoring setups for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize monthly distributions.
Sell high-beta single names like CRWD and broad index QQQ and SMH.
This plan focuses on generating steady income and reducing volatility.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, prioritizing steady distributions. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for lower drawdown, remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
